- Overestimate prices when sentiment is positive (especially >0.27) — model tends to ignore sentiment-driven corrections.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative (especially < -0.16) — model fails to account for bearish momentum.
- Overshoot after sharp price spikes — model reacts too quickly, overcorrecting downward.
- Mean reversion bias: model often holds prices too high in trending upticks, then underestimates subsequent pullback.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts consistently overestimate early in the cycle (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is volatile.
- Lagged sentiment effect: if sentiment turns negative within 3–5 days, model fails to adjust forecast downward sharply enough.
- Avoid “sentiment echo” — model often mirrors recent sentiment without adjusting for structural market fundamentals.
